target: Os bydd y bws yn hwyr, bydda i'n cerdded.
english: If the bus is late, I'll walk.
tip: For a real future condition, Welsh uses the future after ‘os’: ‘os bydd y bws yn hwyr’ (if the bus is late).

target: Byddan nhw'n agor y llyfrgell newydd ym mis Mawrth.
english: They will open the new library in March.
tip: ‘yn’ meaning 'in' becomes ‘ym’ before m: ‘ym mis Mawrth’ (in March).

target: Gofynnodd y plant a allen nhw fynd i'r parc.
english: The children asked if they could go to the park.
tip: ‘a’ introduces an indirect yes-or-no question ('whether'): ‘a allen nhw fynd’ (whether they could go).

target: Mae canu mewn côr yn ffordd wych o wneud ffrindiau a mwynhau cerddoriaeth gyda'i gilydd.
english: Singing in a choir is a wonderful way to make friends and enjoy music together.
tip: Adjectives soften after a feminine singular noun: ‘gwych’ becomes ‘wych’ in ‘ffordd wych’ (a wonderful way).

target: Dyma'r opsiwn rhataf sydd ar gael.
english: It's the cheapest option available.
tip: Add ‘-af’ for the superlative: ‘rhad’ (cheap) becomes ‘rhataf’ (cheapest), as in ‘opsiwn rhataf’.

target: Mae gen i gefnder yn America.
english: I have a cousin in America.
tip: Welsh has no verb 'to have'; ‘mae gen i’ means 'is with me': ‘mae gen i gefnder’ (I have a cousin).

target: Canolbwyntiwch ar eich anadlu wrth fyfyrio.
english: Concentrate on your breathing while meditating.
tip: ‘wrth’ before a verb means 'while doing it': ‘wrth fyfyrio’ (while meditating).

target: Y plant sy'n ei fwynhau fwyaf.
english: It's the children who enjoy it most.
tip: ‘ei’ meaning 'it' softens the next word: ‘mwynhau’ becomes ‘fwynhau’ in ‘ei fwynhau’ (enjoy it).

target: Mae'n amlwg mai'r tywydd sy'n broblem.
english: It's obvious the weather is the problem.
tip: ‘mai’ marks a focused noun inside a 'that' clause: ‘mai'r tywydd sy'n broblem’ (that it's the weather that's the problem).

target: Bydd y newid hinsawdd yn effeithio ar bawb.
english: Climate change will affect everyone.
tip: ‘effeithio’ takes ‘ar’ for 'affect': ‘effeithio ar bawb’ (affect everyone); the ‘ar’ is required.

target: Cyn gynted ag y cyrhaeddais i, dechreuodd y cyfarfod.
english: As soon as I arrived, the meeting began.
tip: ‘cyn gynted ag’ is the set phrase for 'as soon as': ‘cyn gynted ag y cyrhaeddais i’ (as soon as I arrived).

target: Bydda i'n darllen y llyfr yna yn ystod y gwyliau.
english: I will read that book during the holidays.
tip: 'That' follows the noun in Welsh: ‘y llyfr yna’ = that book, with ‘yna’ after what it points to.

target: Pe bai hi'n siarad Cymraeg, gallai hi gael y swydd.
english: If she spoke Welsh, she could get the job.
tip: ‘pe bai’ is 'if' for imagined, unreal situations: ‘pe bai hi'n siarad Cymraeg’ (if she spoke Welsh, but she doesn't).

target: Bydd y canlyniadau'n cael eu cyhoeddi yfory.
english: The results will be announced tomorrow.
tip: Welsh forms the passive with ‘cael’ plus ‘eu’ (their): ‘cael eu cyhoeddi’ means 'get their announcing' = be announced.

target: O flaen y tŷ mae coeden fawr.
english: In front of the house is a big tree.
tip: ‘o flaen’ is a two-word position phrase, 'in front of': ‘o flaen y tŷ mae coeden fawr’ (in front of the house is a tree).

target: Os bydd hi'n astudio meddygaeth, bydd hi'n dod yn feddyg.
english: If she studies medicine, she'll become a doctor.
tip: ‘dod yn’ means 'become' and softens the next word: ‘meddyg’ becomes ‘feddyg’ in ‘dod yn feddyg’.

target: Dylid gwarchod yr amgylchedd.
english: The environment should be protected.
tip: ‘dylid’ means one should or it should be done, with no subject named: ‘dylid gwarchod’ = should be protected.

target: Bydd digon o fwyd.
english: There will be plenty of food.
tip: The word ‘o’ (of) softens the next noun: ‘bwyd’ becomes ‘fwyd’ in ‘digon o fwyd’ (plenty of food).

target: Bydd e'n ein gyrru ni i'r orsaf.
english: He will drive us to the station.
tip: Us wraps the verb as ‘ein ... ni’: ‘ein gyrru ni’ = drive us. The pronoun frames the verb on both sides.

target: Bydd hi'n mynd â'r plant i'r parc.
english: She will take the children to the park.
tip: To take someone you say ‘mynd â’, literally go with: ‘mynd â'r plant’ = take the children.

target: Cerddoriaeth sy'n dod â phobl at ei gilydd.
english: It's music that brings people together.
tip: The word ‘â’ changes the next word's start, p to ph: ‘pobl’ becomes ‘phobl’ in ‘dod â phobl’ (bring people).

target: Bydda i'n dy helpu di gyda'r gwaith cartref.
english: I will help you with the homework.
tip: Your (informal) frames the verb as ‘dy ... di’: ‘dy helpu di’ = help you. Formal or plural uses ‘eich ... chi’ instead.

target: Bydd y gwaith adnewyddu yn cymryd chwe mis.
english: The renovation work will take six months.
tip: After a number Welsh keeps the noun singular: ‘chwe mis’ = six months (month), never a plural.

target: Dw i angen gorffwys am wythnos, meddai'r meddyg.
english: I need to rest for a week, the doctor says.
tip: ‘meddai’ means said or says and reports speech, placed after the quote: ‘meddai'r meddyg’ = the doctor says.

target: Os bydd y trên yn llawn, byddwn ni'n sefyll.
english: If the train is full, we'll stand.
tip: For a future if, Welsh uses ‘bydd’ after ‘os’, not the present: ‘os bydd y trên yn llawn’ = if the train is full.

target: Bydda i'n dy ffonio di pan gyrhaedda i adref.
english: I will call you when I get home.
tip: ‘pan’ (when) softens the verb: ‘cyrhaedda’ becomes ‘gyrhaedda’ in ‘pan gyrhaedda i’ (when I arrive).

target: Os bydd e'n pasio'i brawf, bydd e'n prynu car.
english: If he passes his test, he'll buy a car.
tip: His shortens to ‘'i’ and softens the next word: ‘prawf’ becomes ‘brawf’ in ‘pasio'i brawf’ (pass his test).

target: Pe bawn i'n gwybod, byddwn i wedi dweud wrthot ti.
english: If I had known, I would have told you.
tip: For unreal or hypothetical ifs use ‘pe’ with ‘bawn’, not ‘os’: ‘pe bawn i'n gwybod’ = if I had known.

target: Dywedodd rhywun fod y bws yn hwyr.
english: Someone said the bus was late.
tip: To report that something is, use ‘fod’: ‘dywedodd rhywun fod y bws yn hwyr’ = someone said the bus was late.

target: Bydd hi'n dysgu dosbarth ioga ddydd Mercher.
english: She will teach a yoga class on Wednesday.
tip: To say on a day, soften ‘dydd’ to ‘ddydd’: ‘ddydd Mercher’ = on Wednesday.
